bodyMarkdown:
## Summary

Design governance through delivery is the practice of preserving design intent through development. The practice exists because development creates situations that a design did not anticipate: unmodelled states, implementation constraints, screen-size conditions, business-logic interactions, and edge cases that require decisions.

Without a governance structure, those decisions are made by whoever is available, using local implementation logic. Over time, local decisions accumulate into design fragmentation. Design governance through delivery creates a structure for answering implementation questions before they become design deviations.

The practice has four components: a design system used as a reasoning record, structured support availability, implementation review, and organisational integration. The endpoint is not continued dependence on Creative Navy. The endpoint is a client team that can maintain and extend the design system independently.

## What design governance through delivery does

Design governance through delivery holds design decisions through the build by making the reasoning behind those decisions available to the development team. A component library tells developers what to build. A reasoning record explains why a component, interaction, state, or workflow was designed in a particular way.

The reasoning record is important when developers encounter implementation conditions that were not fully specified. If the design system explains what alternatives were considered, what the design was solving for, and what would break if a decision changed, developers can make decisions aligned with design intent rather than decisions limited to a local implementation context.

Structured support availability ensures that unresolved implementation questions can reach the right person before an independent design decision is made by default. The practice does not require Creative Navy to be present at all times. The operative metric is response time within working hours.

Implementation review compares what has been built with what was designed. The review is diagnostic rather than a quality gate. It identifies where implementation has diverged from design intent, determines whether the cause is an edge case, constraint, or misinterpretation, and supports either implementation correction or design update.

Organisational integration prepares the client team to maintain and extend the design system after Creative Navy's engagement ends. Design governance through delivery therefore treats implementation support as a transition towards independence, not as a subscription service.

## When Creative Navy uses design governance through delivery

Design governance through delivery is used after design delivery and alongside development. It is the practice that makes the Implementation Partnership phase functional rather than nominal.

The practice begins during Organizational Integration, when the design system is prepared for handover and the support structure is established. It continues through implementation until the client team is operating independently.

Design governance through delivery depends on the design work already having been done. It follows design practices rather than replacing them. Its purpose is to maintain the output of the design process through development.

## The design system as governance infrastructure

The design system produced during Organizational Integration is the primary governance tool during Implementation Partnership. Its governance function differs from its implementation function.

As an implementation tool, the design system specifies components, states, interactions, and implementation details. As a governance tool, it records why those decisions were made, what alternatives were considered, and what consequences follow if the decision is changed.

A design system without documented reasoning is an implementation tool only. It may specify a state or component accurately, but it does not help a developer decide what to do when an unanticipated state appears. In that situation, the developer has no basis for choosing the design-consistent decision and is more likely to make a local decision.

Design governance through delivery treats the design system as the main knowledge-transfer vehicle between the design team and the development team. The goal is for the development team to understand the design logic well enough to extend it without recreating the complexity that the design work removed.

## Indicators of successful design governance

Low support ticket volume is a signal that the design system carries enough reasoning to guide implementation. When developers understand why a decision was made, implementation questions are rarer. High ticket volume is a governance warning because it indicates that the design system is not carrying enough reasoning for independent implementation.

Fast response time matters when tickets do arise. Questions that are not answered quickly are often answered by developers making their own decisions. In design governance through delivery, response time is a practical control against design deviation.

Low rework from implementation to design correction indicates that divergences are being found early. Implementation review is intended to identify divergence before correction becomes expensive.

Proactive build reviews initiated by the development team are a strong governance signal. When developers seek review rather than waiting to be reviewed, they have internalised enough of the design standard to recognise when external input is needed.

Client independence at engagement close is the clearest governance measure. The practice is successful when the client team can extend and maintain the design system without Creative Navy support.

## Evidence from multi-year Implementation Partnership engagements

Triopsis workforce management recorded a 2-year Implementation Partnership. The design system included 68 components, 200+ documented states, and 15 workflow type specifications. The governance artefact was designed to answer implementation questions without requiring Creative Navy consultation for every edge case. Client-reported how-can-I support questions fell to approximately 5% of previous volume, and rework from implementation issues was described as minimal.

Polymatica OLAP analytics recorded a 2-year Implementation Partnership with 67 support requests across the full period and an average response time of 2 hours. The low request frequency and response time are governance evidence: the recorded support structure answered questions before developers made independent design decisions. The documented outcome was a design system that the development team could extend to new features without continued input.

Tetra/Prism property compliance recorded a 2-year Implementation Partnership with 12 support tickets total and an average response time of 1 hour. The low ticket volume is evidence that the design system carried enough reasoning for mobile and web implementation edge cases. The documented governance outcome was independent operation at engagement close, with the organisation extending both the mobile app and web platform without Creative Navy involvement.

Pixelart Fugo digital signage CMS recorded a 2-year Implementation Partnership structured as monthly developer show-and-tell sessions. The development team was unfamiliar with the new design system at the start of Implementation Partnership. The sessions created a regular checkpoint for identifying and resolving implementation divergences before they accumulated. Client-measured NPS moved from 57% to 89% pre/post; the source evidence attributes the implemented product quality to governance that kept implementation aligned with design intent.

Gexcon CFD simulation recorded a 2-year Implementation Partnership after a 7-month design execution phase. The purpose of governance was to preserve the new architectural logic during a long development period. The source evidence describes the risk as a return to the accumulated complexity pattern that the redesign had removed.

## Evidence from bounded support and handover-heavy engagements

CDR Foodlab chemical analysis instrument recorded a 7-month Implementation Partnership with 3 developer contacts total. Two contacts were build reviews initiated by the development team, and one was a question session producing approximately 5 questions. The split matters because the build reviews show proactive governance, while the question session indicates the design system's reasoning sufficiency.

The CDR Foodlab deliverable scope before Implementation Partnership included full UX redesign, full UI across the complete screen set, a design system with variant architecture, inline tutorial animations, and a formal handover session with the development team. The low contact volume is consistent with a handover that transferred reasoning as well as specifications. The contact counts and contact types are Creative Navy-observed; the interpretation of what they mean is analytical.

Egma Order, Egma's B2B lens ordering platform, used an unusually specific handover practice. The final session was a training session in operating the design file: developers were taught how to measure padding or gaps, move from an instance to its main component, inspect states, sample colour values, export icons as SVG, and use a plugin to locate component variant usage. Creative Navy also remained reachable in Egma's own workspace for implementation questions. The platform is live, but no post-launch performance measurement is recorded.

The industrial engagement for a European industrial automation vendor has development-ready components implemented, including a status timeline component delivered as documentation plus prototype. Decisions carried an audit trail through numbered tracked design questions and attributed review threads. The product is in development, not shipped, so the engagement is not evidence of a shipped outcome.

## Schone, Raymarine, and maritime VTS as handover and change-control examples

Schone Airspace Group's uncrewed aircraft Mission Control work records all four governance components and an additional decision mechanism. The reasoning record included machine-readable handover alongside written specification: a design token file, component register, screen register, and acceptance ledger, versioned together so component variants, screen content, and state decisions could be checked against one release index.

Schone also records structured support and implementation review. Four exploration sprints converted into a twelve-sprint programme, then into a twelve-month retainer at biweekly involvement. Across seven months, all 54 delivered screens were compared against built software by Creative Navy's design team. Deviations were identified and recorded by name. The product is in test; this is not a deployment claim and not evidence that the design is good.

Schone's additional mechanism was a handover protocol that separated proposed changes into changes requiring UX approval and changes requiring engineering review. It also specified a build sequence that placed the shared command shell and immutable aircraft and request identities before other work. This is governance expressed as a decision procedure rather than only as an availability promise.

Raymarine's next-generation fixed-mount VHF engagement recorded a lighter but structurally related mechanism. A two-class change-control rule issued with handover identified four proposals that reopen a recorded UX decision: remapping the channel encoder, removing routine recipient confirmation, merging incident statuses, or permitting automatic network-initiated radio actions. Each requires a documented impact assessment. The radio was built and released, but no design-fidelity comparison is recorded.

Maritime VTS recorded governance beginning at a gate. Three decision options were defined in advance: proceed, revise the reference product or scope, or stop and retain the discovery package as a self-contained strategic deliverable. Approval was conditional, with seven release conditions carrying named client owners and verification methods. The governance model that followed used a four-layer architecture in which applications consume semantic tokens and documented components and do not redefine them. The client wrote the code and Creative Navy supplied standard implementation support. The design system reached production; no design-fidelity comparison is recorded.

## AIT, the MDU, and Assemblio as three fidelity mechanisms

AIT is an example of design surviving development through a recorded governance mechanism. Implementation Partnership was five months of support to AIT's engineering team during development, consisting of three scheduled progress meetings where development state was shared and compared against delivered designs, plus eight support tickets answered. The controller reached the market months after the engagement ended. Creative Navy compared the shipped interface against the delivered designs, and the product ships as the design that was delivered. It ships in a touch-only hardware configuration. The move to touch-only was AIT's hardware decision, not a Creative Navy outcome.

AIT's governance infrastructure also included a design system built for controlled variation. The interface was delivered in three complete themes: two AIT consumer brands and a neutral OEM theme. Brand difference was confined to colour, while structure, layout, and components remained identical. The design system included a single-typeface typography scale, 24 px and 48 px icon sets, and a component library covering home widgets and their states, alerts, keyboard keys, progress-indicator tabs, a breadcrumb trail, a scenario timeline, selectors, a circle loader, and a serial-number input.

The MDU, a ship motion monitoring product whose manufacturer is not named, is a second case where the product shipped and the design was implemented as delivered. The governance instrument differs from AIT. Creative Navy briefed each of the third-party development agencies the manufacturer was considering, so that each candidate pitched on a common understanding of the delivered design. The fidelity outcome is recorded, but the cause is not established because the shape of implementation support is not recorded.

Assemblio is a third variant. Composer and Smart Viewer were supported by one session and eight support tickets, making this a question-answering arrangement rather than build oversight. The product is in production, and Creative Navy compared the shipped interface against the delivered designs: the Composer, the Smart Viewer, the platform around them, and sync profiles ship as the design that was delivered. Assemblio's developers built from the documented components. The handover included 93 components, every component documented with all states, design tokens carrying light and dark themes, and component documentation carrying reasoning as well as specification. The outcome is consistent with the handover, but no development speed, cost, or defect-rate measurement is recorded.

## Boundary between design governance and design quality claims

Design governance through delivery is evidence that a design survived development only where fidelity evidence exists. It is not, by itself, evidence that the design is good, that the product performed well after launch, or that commercial results followed.

On this page, the shipped or production fidelity claim applies only to AIT, the MDU, and Assemblio, where Creative Navy verified the comparison. Schone has a different evidence form: all 54 delivered screens were compared against built software across seven months and deviations were named. Raymarine and maritime VTS do not have recorded fidelity comparisons.

Client-reported outcomes remain client-reported. Triopsis ticket-volume reduction, Bofin mid-sprint clarification reduction, Bofin reduced rework, and Bofin deadline performance are reported by the client. Pixelart Fugo's NPS movement is client-measured. These evidence bases should not be treated as independent measurement.

Some engagements record support structure without recording its weight. Raymarine and maritime VTS record that Creative Navy offered or supplied implementation support, but the duration, form, frequency, review count, and ticket count are not recorded. Those values should not be borrowed from other engagements.

## Relationship to design system boundary definition

Design governance through delivery is about holding a design through a build. Design system boundary definition is a related but different practice: it is about deciding what may be shared before the build starts.

The distinction matters because governance relies on boundaries already being defined. A development team can only preserve a shared design logic if the design system explains which decisions are shared, which decisions are product-specific, and where product deviation requires approval.
